invariants.text: A credential request has exactly one final authoritative result.
Every crash recovers to a complete commit or complete rollback.
Ambiguous authority state fails closed and never guesses success.
The same requestId and mutation is never executed twice.
The same requestId with a different mutation is rejected as a conflict.
Vault, metadata, journal, SQLite, AppRuntime and SecureBridge projections are mutually verifiable.
Any credential decryption failure rejects the complete hydration.
Missing, damaged, truncated or illegal journal history is never treated as empty history.
A backend with unknown credential generation cannot remain RUNNING.
Every vault mutation uses one serialized CredentialVaultHost coordinator.
Every desktop credential start, stop, restart, mutation, migration, reset, crash recovery and shutdown transition is serialized by one application lease.
A desktop credential mutation cannot begin until the old backend has emitted a real exit and owner-exit recovery has completed.
A failed or unconfirmed stop leaves vault bytes, authority digest, generation and transaction history unchanged and never returns UI success.
Application shutdown cannot cross the mutation commit boundary or start a replacement owner.
A mutation committed before restart failure is never re-executed; the same requestId performs durable replay only.
New-owner success requires exact vault epoch, generation, authority event, authority digest, counts, FD5, READY, FD6, SQLite, AppRuntime and SecureBridge agreement.
A new owner rejected by READY or runtime projection validation is terminated and owner-exit recovery completes before fail-safe return.
An interrupted application lifecycle journal is detected and resumed fail-safely rather than discarded.
Desktop UI success is returned only after the new owner and all runtime authority projections are ready.
